entries.title: Windows page file (pagefile.sys)
entries.what: Windows' overflow memory: when RAM is full, it moves things here.
entries.safetyText: Windows is using it right now. You can change its size, but don't delete it.
entries.whyBig: Windows sizes it to your RAM, often 8-32 GB.
howTo: Settings › System › About › Advanced system settings › Performance Settings › Advanced › Virtual memory › Change.

entries.title: Windows hibernation file (hiberfil.sys)
entries.what: Where Windows saves memory when it hibernates or uses Fast Startup.
entries.safetyText: Don't delete it; turn hibernation off instead and Windows removes it (Fast Startup stops working).
entries.whyBig: It's sized to a large part of your RAM.
howTo: Open a Command Prompt as administrator.

entries.title: Windows swap file (swapfile.sys)
entries.what: Used by Windows for Store apps' memory.
entries.safetyText: Managed by Windows together with the page file.

entries.title: Windows memory dump (MEMORY.DMP)
entries.what: Saved when Windows crashed with a blue screen, for diagnosis.
entries.safetyText: Safe once you don't need to investigate that crash (Disk Cleanup removes it too).

entries.title: Previous Windows installation (Windows.old)
entries.what: Your old Windows, kept after an upgrade so you can go back for about 10 days.
entries.safetyText: Remove it with Windows' own cleanup (it has protected files that resist normal deletion).
entries.whyBig: It's a whole copy of the previous Windows: 10-30 GB.
howTo: Settings › System › Storage › Temporary files › Previous Windows installation(s).

entries.title: Windows component store (WinSxS)
entries.what: Every version of Windows' system components, for updates and repairs. Many files are shared, so its real size is smaller than Explorer shows.
entries.safetyText: Never delete from it; let Windows clean superseded updates.

entries.title: Windows Installer cache (C:\Windows\Installer)
entries.what: Copies of installers Windows needs to repair, update or uninstall programs.
entries.safetyText: Deleting these breaks updating and uninstalling programs.

entries.title: Delivery Optimization cache
entries.what: Windows Update pieces shared with other PCs.
entries.safetyText: Clear it with Disk Cleanup (Delivery Optimization Files).
howTo: Settings › System › Storage › Temporary files › Delivery Optimization Files.

entries.title: Recycle Bin
entries.what: Things you (or Miu) deleted, kept so they can be restored.
entries.safetyText: Empty it when you're sure; that's when the space really comes back.
howTo: Right-click the Recycle Bin › Empty Recycle Bin.

entries.title: System Volume Information
entries.what: Restore points and file history snapshots.
entries.safetyText: Manage restore points from System Protection, not by deleting files.
howTo: Search ‘Create a restore point’ › Configure › Delete, or lower Max Usage.

entries.title: .DS_Store
entries.what: Finder's per-folder view settings (icon positions, sort order).
entries.safetyText: Finder recreates it when you open the folder.

entries.title: Thumbs.db / desktop.ini
entries.what: Windows' picture thumbnails and folder settings.
entries.safetyText: Windows recreates them as needed.

entries.title: Time Machine local snapshots
entries.what: Snapshots macOS keeps on your disk until your backup drive is connected again.
entries.safetyText: macOS deletes them automatically when space runs low; you can also remove them.

entries.title: iPhone / iPad backups
entries.what: Device backups made by Finder or iTunes.
entries.safetyText: These may be your only backup of a phone. Delete old ones from Finder or iTunes, not by hand.
entries.whyBig: Each backup holds a whole device's data.
howTo: Finder › your iPhone › Manage Backups (or iTunes › Preferences › Devices).

entries.title: Homebrew cache
entries.what: Downloaded bottles and source for brew installs.
entries.safetyText: Let brew remove what it doesn't need.

entries.title: systemd journal
entries.what: System logs on Linux.
entries.safetyText: Shrink it with journalctl rather than deleting files.

entries.title: Flatpak runtimes
entries.what: Shared runtimes for Flatpak apps.
entries.safetyText: Remove the ones no app uses.

entries.title: Old Snap revisions
entries.what: Snap keeps older revisions of each app so it can roll back.
entries.safetyText: Remove disabled revisions with snap.

entries.title: Log file
entries.what: Text a program writes about what it's doing, for troubleshooting.
entries.safetyText: Old logs are safe to remove; programs start a new one. A log that keeps growing usually means debug logging was left on.

entries.title: Installer
entries.what: A setup file you downloaded (.exe, .msi, .dmg, .pkg, .deb, .rpm).
entries.safetyText: Once the program is installed you usually don't need it; you can download it again.

entries.title: Disk image (.iso / .img)
entries.what: A copy of a whole CD/DVD/USB disk, often an operating system installer.
entries.safetyText: Safe if you can download it again or no longer need it. Check that it isn't a virtual machine's disk.

entries.title: Virtual machine disk
entries.what: The hard disk of a virtual machine (VirtualBox, VMware, Hyper-V, UTM, Parallels).
entries.safetyText: Deleting it deletes that whole virtual computer. Remove the VM from its app if you don't need it.

entries.title: Crash reports
entries.what: Reports apps saved when they crashed.
entries.safetyText: Only useful to investigate those crashes.
